SELECT
  u.full_name AS rep_name,
  t.name AS merchant,
  COUNT(*) AS opportunities_closed,
  SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_won,
  SUM(CASE WHEN NOT o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_lost,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.is_won THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.closed_at - o.created_at)) / 86400.0), 1) AS avg_days_open,
  ROUND(AVG(
    CASE WHEN o.currency_code = 'EUR' THEN o.amount
    ELSE o.amount / (
      SELECT er.rate
      FROM exchange_rates er
      WHERE er.base_code = 'EUR'
        AND er.quote_code = o.currency_code
        AND er.as_of = CAST(o.closed_at AS date)
    ) END
  ), 2) AS avg_amount_eur
FROM opportunities o
JOIN users u ON u.id = o.owner_user_id
JOIN tenants t ON t.id = o.tenant_id
JOIN pipelines pl ON pl.id = o.pipeline_id AND pl.tenant_id = o.tenant_id
WHERE o.is_closed = true
  AND pl.name = 'New business'
  AND o.tenant_id IN (
    SELECT tn.id FROM tenants tn WHERE tn.industry IN ('industrial supplies', 'office equipment')
  )
GROUP BY o.owner_user_id, u.full_name, t.name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY win_rate_pct ASC, opportunities_closed DESC, rep_name ASC
note: I used tenants.industry IN ('industrial supplies','office equipment') as the B2B wholesale tenant filter and pipelines.name = 'New business' as the pipeline filter, matching the verticals and pipeline naming convention described for this series of reports — please confirm these match the exact filter used in the earlier merchant-level report if it differed. The exact count of reps excluded by the <3 closed-deals rule isn't a value I can compute at authoring time (dry runs don't return data); it will be visible as the gap between total distinct owners in scope and the row count printed on this report.
